mentl/017dc4d:
The trial is the sizing oracle: each stmt's mint count is the
graph_next delta around its trial inference, and the final pass mints
each stmt into a pre-assigned dense range [base, base+count) with
bases prefix-summed from the final's own post-prepass frontier. The
numbering is a pure function of the source through the trial's
determinism — exactly what the parallel fan must reproduce, which is
its byte-equality gate. Three graph ops carry the plan (mint_plan
seeds the overflow target, mint_at enters a range and raises the
high-water, mint_seal resumes sequential); a mint at a range's
ceiling jumps deterministically to the open space above the plan; an
under-measure stmt leaves virgin gap cells absorbed by the word-face
guard now on graph_node_at. Handle space stays dense: the partition
is a numbering plan over the paged spine, decoupled from storage —
no sparse encoding, no iterator migration.

mentl/0116d5d:
First substrate of incremental compilation. KaiFile record per H2
discipline; FNV-1a 32-bit source hash; textual v1 serialization;
read/write through the Filesystem effect (FS substrate landed
just before).

KaiFile shape (alphabetically sorted per parser invariant):
  compiler_version  — bumps on format change; mismatch = cache miss
  exported_entries  — STUB in IC.1a (empty); IC.1b serializes env
  imports           — STUB in IC.1a; IC.1b extracts from ImportStmt
  imports_hashes    — STUB in IC.1a; IC.1b for downstream invalidation
  module_name       — qualified module path
  source_hash       — FNV-1a 32-bit over source bytes

Hash: FNV-1a (offset 2166136261, prime 16777619). Not cryptographic
— adequate for cache invalidation. Collision means rare stale
return on a changed-but-same-hash edit; subsequent dep invalidation
catches it.

Path convention: <project>/.inka/cache/<module>.kai with module
slashes flattened to `__` so filenames stay flat. cache_dir() and
cache_path_for(module_name) define the canonical location.

Format (textual v1 — binary in IC.1c if measured):
  INKA-KAI v<n>
  module:<name>
  hash:<decimal>
  imports:
  entries:

cache_serialize / cache_deserialize round-trip the header. Body
fields (imports, entries) are line markers IC.1b fills with real
serialized data; IC.1a's parser tolerates them as empty.

Public API:
  cache_write(kai)            with Filesystem    — mkdir -p + write
  cache_read(module_name)     with Filesystem    — Option<KaiFile>
  cache_is_hit(kai, source)                      — version + hash check

cache_is_hit answers ONLY "is this source byte-identical to when we
wrote this cache?". Dependency-hash invalidation (cache hit on M
requires every dep's recorded imports_hashes match dep's current
source_hash) lives at IC.2 driver level.

Helpers all bounded by source size; minimal text parsing via
runtime/strings primitives (str_eq, str_slice, byte_at, byte_len,
int_to_str, parse_int).

Honest scoping: IC.1a gives the drive

mentl/01aa77d:
Crucible 5: apply(double, 21) = 42. Function table, type signatures per arity, call_indirect for indirect calls. Functions as first-class values.

Crucible 6: add5(10) = 15. Closure objects on heap [fn_idx:i32][count:i32][upvals...]. LUpval emission loads from closure pointer. Captured variables detected via Pure scope-tracking tree walk, rewritten via Pure LowIR transform. No effect operations for captures -- the crash taught us: if the answer depends only on the subtree, it's a Pure transform.

Uniform calling convention: every function gets __closure as first param. Direct calls pass 0. Closures pass the pointer. No special cases at call sites. is_global added to LowerCtx to distinguish globals from captures.
sonido/015f4d1:
Rework the graph editor's Input/Output into full-height wall bars welded to
the canvas edges — each bar is the in/out meter, the wire anchor, and carries
its gain/master knob at the foot — on desktop and phone alike. Plus three
graph-UX fixes from the phone audit.

Wall bars (graph_view.rs + app.rs):
- Capture the live pan/zoom transform via the public Viewport handed to a new
  SnarlViewer::draw_background override (SnarlState itself is private).
- pin_io_nodes() welds the Input/Output pins to the screen walls each frame
  using that transform, so I/O can never be panned off-screen.
- render_io_bar draws each wall as a vertical LevelMeter + foot knob; the old
  side I/O strips (render_io_strip) and phone levels row (render_phone_levels)
  are removed and the central layout is now a full-width canvas flanked by the
  two bars, unified across desktop and phone.
- Zoom is bounded via SnarlStyle min/max scale (the "weird resizing" report).
  Mid-canvas pan stays free (egui-snarl keeps the pan offset private; double-
  click recenters) — welded I/O is the real fix for the off-screen complaint.

Bundled fixes:
- Duplicate/Remove: guard show()'s empty-space deselect against presses over a
  foreground overlay, so tapping the touch action bar no longer deselects the
  node before the button can act.
- Add button always appends the new effect as the sole Output feeder
  (append_before_output), rerouting every prior Output-feeder into it; right-
  click-on-wire keeps its positional splice.
- Focus mode now hides the morph band + Info View (the I/O strips it used to
  hide are gone); the thin wall bars stay.

Tests: add-merge absorption and the wall→graph pin mapping round-trip.
